Vision search: CLIP vs Gemini Embedding 2

GVSU Art Museum · image-similarity retrieval over 34,098 indexed works · 12 August 2026

What this is. Ten well-known public-domain paintings outside of the GVSU collection, submitted to both services. Each returns the nearest visually similar results. No query has a “correct” answer in the catalogue. So this is a measure of how each model generalizes, not on their accuracy.

The finding. The two models agree on only 1.7 of 10 results on average. They are not interchangeable. Replacing the model essentially swaps out all results. However, the new results may be more visually similar, as is the case with The Great Wave which returns more woodblock landscapes and fewer portraits. Results shared by both are outlined in blue.

Method & limitations

  • Query images came from Wikimedia Commons at 900 px and were posted unmodified to POST /search on both services, which share an identical request and response contract.
  • Both indexes cover the same catalogue. The previous service self-retrieved 11 of 12 sampled GVSU works at rank 1, so its coverage is comparable rather than a partial slice.
  • There is no ground truth here. None of these paintings are in the collection, so neither service can be scored as right or wrong. They can only be compared. Taste is a human trait after all.
  • Latency includes uploading a 170–500 kB image over the public internet; it is not model inference time.
  • The previous service returned a duplicate row in 4 of 10 queries. The embeddings table currently does not have a unique constraint on object_id.
